claims.source: Although the cytotoxic effects induced by this compound have been related to rDNA-transcription inhibition (Mars et al., 2020; Negi and Brown, 2015), CX-5461 has also been shown to be a potent G4 stabilizer and to provoke rapid induction of DSBs through a TOP2-dependent mechanism (Bruno et al., 2020; Olivieri et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: CX-5461 provokes rapid induction of DSBs through a TOP2-dependent mechanism.
claims.source: Although the cytotoxic effects induced by this compound have been related to rDNA-transcription inhibition (Mars et al., 2020; Negi and Brown, 2015), CX-5461 has also been shown to be a potent G4 stabilizer and to provoke rapid induction of DSBs through a TOP2-dependent mechanism (Bruno et al., 2020; Olivieri et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Human near haploid HAP1 cells were randomly mutagenized with ethyl methane sulfonate (EMS) to select CX-5461-resistant clones.
claims.source: To do this, human near haploid HAP1 cells were randomly mutagenized with ethyl methane sulfonate (EMS) based on previous work (Forment et al., 2017) and clones resistant to a lethal CX-5461 concentration of 0.3 µM were isolated (CX-5461-resistant [CXR] clones).
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claims.claim: Seven CXR clones showed IC50 values for CX-5461 ranging from 0.22 to 0.34 µM, corresponding to an average ninefold increase compared to wild-type HAP1 cells.
claims.source: Resistance of seven of these clones to CX-5461 was further confirmed by cell survival assays showing IC50 values on CXR clones ranging from 0.22 to 0.34 µM CX-5461, corresponding to an average ninefold increase in the IC50 value compared to the 0.03 µM IC50 on wild-type HAP1 cells (WT) (see Figure 1A and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: CXR clones did not show cross-resistance to nocodazole, excluding a multidrug resistance (MDR) phenotype.
claims.source: In addition, CXR clones did not show cross-resistance to the unrelated drug and efflux-pumps substrate nocodazole (Kasap et al., 2014), excluding a multidrug resistance (MDR) phenotype (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding that excludes an alternative explanation for the resistance phenotype.

claims.claim: TOP2A emerged as the only gene with coding mutations in all CXR clones.
claims.source: From these analyses, TOP2A emerged as the only gene with coding mutations in all resistant clones.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNA-seq analysis of CXR clones.

claims.claim: Four CXR clones had a mutation in the ATPase domain of TOP2A (F85I).
claims.source: Four clones had a mutation in the ATPase domain (F85I), while two had mutations in the DNA-binding region (S654N and L703I) (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the sequencing analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Two CXR clones had mutations in the DNA-binding region of TOP2A (S654N and L703I).
claims.source: Four clones had a mutation in the ATPase domain (F85I), while two had mutations in the DNA-binding region (S654N and L703I) (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the sequencing analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: None of the identified TOP2A mutations resulted in the loss of TOP2A protein.
claims.source: Immunoblotting analysis revealed that none of the identified TOP2A mutations resulted in the loss of TOP2A protein, in agreement with its essential function in proliferating cells (Akimitsu et al., 2003; Carpenter and Porter, 2004).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunoblotting analysis.

claims.claim: TOP2B expression level was unaffected in CXR clones.
claims.source: In addition, TOP2B expression level was unaffected in these clones (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunoblotting analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: All CXR clones presented strong resistance to etoposide (ETP) with resistance indexes ranging from 8- to 19-fold relative to control cells.
claims.source: All CXR presented a strong resistance to ETP with resistance indexes ranging from 8- to 19-fold relative to control cells (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: TOP2A point mutations in CXR clones reduce TOP2A activity.
claims.source: These results support the idea that TOP2A point mutations in CXR clones reduce TOP2A activity.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the resistance to etoposide, a TOP2 poison.

claims.claim: Point mutations in clones CXR #A6 and CXR #A1 decrease the amount of TOP2Acc following ETP treatment.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1, the point mutations present in clones CXR #A6 and CXR #A1 decrease the amount of TOP2Acc following ETP treatment.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from the heparin-based extraction assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Five F14R clones carried five different TOP2A mutations.
claims.source: Targeted sequencing of TOP2A cDNA in five F14R clones revealed five different TOP2A mutations, confirming that TOP2A is the main mediator of F14512 cytotoxicity (Bombarde et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from targeted sequencing of F14R clones.

claims.claim: TOP2A is the main mediator of F14512 cytotoxicity.
claims.source: Targeted sequencing of TOP2A cDNA in five F14R clones revealed five different TOP2A mutations, confirming that TOP2A is the main mediator of F14512 cytotoxicity (Bombarde et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a finding that confirms previous work cited.

claims.claim: All TOP2A mutations in F14R clones were different from those found in CXR clones.
claims.source: All of these mutations were different from the ones found in the CXR clones, which suggests that, despite both acting through TOP2A, CX-54161 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently
claims.evidence: This is an observation from comparing the mutations in CXR and F14R clones.

claims.claim: CX-5461 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently.
claims.source: All of these mutations were different from the ones found in the CXR clones, which suggests that, despite both acting through TOP2A, CX-54161 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the different mutation patterns in CXR and F14R clones.

claims.claim: All F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461.
claims.source: Strikingly, cell survival assays clearly demonstrated that all of the F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461 (Figure 2D), while showing no resistance to nocodazole (Supplementary file 1), with IC50 values for CX-5461 3.6- to 16.8-fold higher than the IC50 value of CX-5461 in WT cells (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1), supporting the concept that the TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones also conferred resistance to the G4 ligand CX-5461.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones conferred resistance to CX-5461.
claims.source: Strikingly, cell survival assays clearly demonstrated that all of the F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461 (Figure 2D), while showing no resistance to nocodazole (Supplementary file 1), with IC50 values for CX-5461 3.6- to 16.8-fold higher than the IC50 value of CX-5461 in WT cells (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1), supporting the concept that the TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones also conferred resistance to the G4 ligand CX-5461.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the cross-resistance data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Population doubling time determination of five clones carrying different TOP2A mutations revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate compared to WT cells.
claims.source: Importantly, population doubling time determination of five clones carrying different TOP2A mutations and flow cytometry analyses of 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation in CXR #A6 and F14R #C1 cells revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate of TOP2A mutated clones as compared to WT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B.

claims.claim: The survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to camptothecin or calicheamicin was not significantly different.
claims.source: In addition, the survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to camptothecin, a DNA TOP1 poison, or calicheamicin, a radio-mimetic compound, was not significantly different.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays.

claims.claim: DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells.
claims.source: Since camptothecin induces toxic replication-associated DSBs, which are mainly repaired by HR, while calicheamicin induces DSB in all cell cycle phases, which are repaired by both NHEJ and HR (Elmroth et al., 2003; Furuta et al., 2003), these results indicate that DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the survival data to different DNA damaging agents.

claims.claim: The sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells.
claims.source: Supporting this conclusion, the sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of the NHEJ factor DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and the kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation measured by flow cytometry analysis of the γH2AX signal were identical between WT and mutant cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from sensitization assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claims.claim: The kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation were identical between WT and TOP2A mutant cells.
claims.source: Supporting this conclusion, the sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of the NHEJ factor DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and the kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation measured by flow cytometry analysis of the γH2AX signal were identical between WT and mutant cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: TOP1 levels were unaffected in TOP2A mutated cells.
claims.source: Finally, western blot analysis showed that TOP1 levels were unaffected in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claims.claim: The resistance to CX-5461 observed in CXR and F14R cells is not associated with major changes in proliferation or DNA repair mechanisms.
claims.source: Altogether, these results indicate that the resistance to CX-5461 observed in CXR and F14R cells is not associated with major changes in proliferation or DNA repair mechanisms.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings.

claims.claim: All CXR clones were cross-resistant to PDS with IC50 values 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher than WT cells.
claims.source: Cell survival assays showed that all CXR clones were cross-resistant to PDS (IC50 values for PDS 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher than the IC50 value of PDS on WT cells) but with lower resistance indexes than those observed for CX-5461 and F14512 (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: All F14R clones were resistant to PDS.
claims.source: More remarkably, cross-resistance studies established that all F14R clones were also resistant to PDS (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Small-interfering RNA-mediated depletion of TOP2A in HAP1 cells conferred marked resistance to CX-5461, PDS, and ETP.
claims.source: The role of TOP2A in the cytotoxicity of CX-5461 and PDS was further supported by the marked resistance to both CX-5461, PDS, and ETP (as a control) conferred by small-interfering RNA-mediated depletion of TOP2A in HAP1 cells, with IC50 values similar to those observed for mutant cells (Figure 2G).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2G.

claims.claim: TOP2A mutant cells do not have significantly different modifications in response to RHPS4 and PhenDC3 compared to WT cells.
claims.source: Through performing cell viability with RPHPS4 and PhenDC3, we revealed that the TOP2A mutant cells do not have significantly different modifications in response to these two chemically unrelated ligands as compared to WT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell viability assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2G.

claims.claim: TOP2A is specifically involved in the cytotoxic effect induced by the two G4 stabilizers CX-5461 and PDS.
claims.source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A is specifically involved in the cytotoxic effect induced by the two G4 stabilizers CX-5461 and PDS.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings showing selective resistance to CX-5461 and PDS but not other G4 ligands.

claims.claim: Short treatments with PDS or CX-5461 induce rapid production of γH2AX and 53BP1 foci in human cells.
claims.source: In human cells, short treatments with PDS or CX-5461 induce rapid production of the DSB markers γH2AX and 53BP1 foci (Rodriguez et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2017; Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations and confirmed by data shown in figures.

claims.claim: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441.
claims.source: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441 (DNA-PKi; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), indicating that a substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway, the major DSB repair pathway in human cells (Pannunzio et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunofluorescence studies shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: A substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway.
claims.source: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441 (DNA-PKi; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), indicating that a substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway, the major DSB repair pathway in human cells (Pannunzio et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the increased γH2AX signal when NHEJ is inhibited.

claims.claim: In CXR cells carrying different mutations in TOP2A, γH2AX production was significantly reduced compared to control cells.
claims.source: First, in CXR cells carrying different mutations in the TOP2A protein, clones CXR #A1 (F85I), #A2 (S654N), and #A6 (intron retention), γH2AX production was significantly reduced as compared to control cells (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunofluorescence studies shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with PDS and CX-5461.
claims.source: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with both G4 ligands, thereby demonstrating the major role of TOP2 catalytic activity in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunofluorescence studies with the TOP2 inhibitor BNS-22.

claims.claim: TOP2 catalytic activity plays a major role in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
claims.source: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with both G4 ligands, thereby demonstrating the major role of TOP2 catalytic activity in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the BNS-22 inhibitor experiments.

claims.claim: In TOP2A-depleted cells, γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence studies showed that in TOP2A-depleted cells γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment and strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: In TOP2A-depleted cells, γH2AX production was strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence studies showed that in TOP2A-depleted cells γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment and strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment.
claims.source: In contrast, TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment, while it reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent to that induced by TOP2A depletion.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments.

claims.claim: TOP2B depletion reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent as TOP2A depletion.
claims.source: In contrast, TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment, while it reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent to that induced by TOP2A depletion.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments.

claims.claim: Simultaneous siRNA-mediated knock-down of TOP2A and TOP2B further decreased γH2AX production by CX-5461 compared to separate siRNAs.
claims.source: Moreover, simultaneous siRNA-mediated knock-down of TOP2A and TOP2B further decreased γH2AX production by CX-5461 when compared to the effect of separate siRNAs (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from double siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells.
claims.source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells, with TOP2B variably contributing depending on the ligand class.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings from TOP2A and TOP2B depletion studies.

claims.claim: TOP2B variably contributes to DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands depending on the ligand class.
claims.source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells, with TOP2B variably contributing depending on the ligand class.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the differential effects of TOP2B depletion on PDS vs CX-5461.

claims.claim: ETP provoked a strong increase in TOP2A signal that correlated with a similar increase in γH2AX foci.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4A, B, ETP provoked a strong increase in TOP2A signal that correlated with a similar increase in γH2AX foci (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from the heparin-based extraction immunofluorescence assay shown in Figure 4A, B.

claims.claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals.
claims.source: Using the same approach, we observed a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals in cells treated with CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B), supporting the idea that these G4 ligands mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from the heparin-based extraction immunofluorescence assay shown in Figure 4A, B.

claims.claim: CX-5461 and PDS mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
claims.source: Using the same approach, we observed a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals in cells treated with CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B), supporting the idea that these G4 ligands mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observed increase in TOP2Acc upon G4 ligand treatment.

claims.claim: 360A is a potent and selective G4 binder that exhibits a lack of clastogenic activity in most human cells compared to CX-5461 and PDS.
claims.source: The bisquinolinium compound 360A is a potent and selective G4 binder that exhibits a lack of clastogenic activity in most human cells as compared to CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of 360A and shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4B (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: 360A pre-treatment did not impact the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4B (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γH2AX signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands.
claims.source: As expected, inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γHA2X signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: 360A pre-treatment did not impact the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells.
claims.source: As expected, inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γHA2X signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing with TOP2Acc.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4C (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C ), CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing (Figure 4D) with TOP2Acc and induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from 3D-SIM colocalization studies shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4C (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C ), CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing (Figure 4D) with TOP2Acc and induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from 3D-SIM colocalization studies shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The increase in TOP2Acc-G4 colocalizations was not observed in ETP-treated cells.
claims.source: It is noteworthy that the increase in TOP2Acc-G4 colocalizations was not observed in ETP-treated cells, showing that the percentage of colocalization does not result from a global increase of TOP2Acc or BG4 signals induced by the different treatments (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from 3D-SIM colocalization studies shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The increased BG4 signal observed in ETP-treated cells probably results from a global increase of DNA supercoiling by ETP.
claims.source: The increased BG4 signal observed in ETP-treated cells probably results from a global increase of DNA supercoiling by ETP, which would promote G4 formation as shown in several other studies (Sekibo and Fox, 2017; Sun, 2010; Sun and Hurley, 2009).
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on previous literature about ETP effects on DNA supercoiling.

claims.claim: TOP2-dependent DSBs induced by CX-5461 and PDS are associated with G4 structures in cells.
claims.source: Altogether, our data support the conclusion that TOP2-dependent DSBs induced by CX-5461 and PDS are associated with G4 structures in cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the colocalization studies and competition experiments.

claims.claim: PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases.
claims.source: We observed that PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases, indicating that PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell cycle analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent.
claims.source: We observed that PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases, indicating that PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that DSB markers appear in all cell cycle phases.

claims.claim: DNA damage induction by PDS and CX-5461 occurs outside of S phase.
claims.source: Using the DNA-base analog EdU to visualize DNA synthesis, we confirmed that DNA damage induction by PDS and CX-5461 also occurs outside of S phase (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from EdU incorporation studies shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: DNA replication-independent processes are very efficient for the production of DSBs by PDS.
claims.source: Furthermore, comparison of the number of G4 ligand-induced γH2AX foci in EdU-negative cells and in the total cell population indicated that DNA replication-independent processes were very efficient for the production of DSBs by PDS (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of γH2AX foci in EdU-negative vs total cells shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: DSB production by PDS in HeLa cells was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription by DRB.
claims.source: Accordingly, DSB production by PDS in HeLa cells was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription by 5,6-dichloro-1-b-D-ribofuranosylbenzimidazole (DRB), an inhibitor of critical phosphorylations in the RNA-Pol-II C-terminal domain (Yankulov et al., 1995; Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from DRB inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription did not impede the accumulation of G4 structures caused by PDS treatment.
claims.source: Importantly, immunofluorescence analysis with the G4-specific antibody BG4 showed that inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription did not impede the accumulation of G4 structures caused by PDS treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from BG4 immunofluorescence studies shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: DRB treatment significantly reduced the formation of γH2AX signals induced by CX-5461 treatment.
claims.source: DRB also reduced DSB production upon CX-5461 treatment, albeit to a lesser extent than with PDS (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from DRB inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Pre-treatment with BMH21 significantly reduced the formation of γH2AX signals induced by CX-5461 treatment.
claims.source: In HeLa cells, pre-treatment with BMH21 significantly reduced the formation of γH2AX signals induced by CX-5461 treatment (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from BMH21 inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Concomitant inhibition of RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I-dependent transcription strongly reduced DSB production by CX-5461.
claims.source: Remarkably, the concomitant inhibition of RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I-dependent transcription strongly reduced DSB production by this compound (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from combined DRB and BMH21 inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Transcription plays a key role in the production of DSBs following the stabilization of G4 structures by PDS and CX-5461.
claims.source: Altogether, these data support a key role of transcription in the production of DSBs following the stabilization of G4 structures by PDS and CX-5461.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the transcription inhibitor experiments.

claims.claim: CX-5461 and PDS provoke a rapid accumulation of R-loops in human cells.
claims.source: In human cells, CX-5461 and PDS have been shown to provoke a rapid accumulation of R-loops (De Magis et al., 2019; Sanij et al., 2020; Shen et al., 2017; Duquette et al., 2004), which have been associated with the production of transcription-dependent DSBs and genomic instability (De Magis et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: R-loops have been associated with the production of transcription-dependent DSBs and genomic instability.
claims.source: In human cells, CX-5461 and PDS have been shown to provoke a rapid accumulation of R-loops (De Magis et al., 2019; Sanij et al., 2020; Shen et al., 2017; Duquette et al., 2004), which have been associated with the production of transcription-dependent DSBs and genomic instability (De Magis et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Upon RNaseHI expression, there was a significant decrease of DNA damage signals induced by PDS and CX-5461.
claims.source: Upon RNaseHI expression, we observed a significant decrease of DNA damage signals induced by PDS and CX-5461 (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2E), indicating that the production of R-loop structures contributes to the formation of DNA breaks following G4 stabilization.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNaseHI overexpression studies shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: The production of R-loop structures contributes to the formation of DNA breaks following G4 stabilization.
claims.source: Upon RNaseHI expression, we observed a significant decrease of DNA damage signals induced by PDS and CX-5461 (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2E), indicating that the production of R-loop structures contributes to the formation of DNA breaks following G4 stabilization.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the RNaseHI overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: Transcription elongation plays a key role in the production of DNA damage by both G4 ligands.
claims.source: Altogether, these results indicate that transcription elongation plays a key role in the production of DNA damage by both G4 ligands.

results.result: Through EMS mutagenesis of haploid HAP1 cells and selection for CX-5461 resistance, the authors identified TOP2A as the only gene with coding mutations in all seven resistant clones. Four clones had the F85I mutation in the ATPase domain, two had mutations in the DNA-binding region (S654N and L703I), and one had an intron retention mutation. None of the mutations resulted in loss of TOP2A protein, and TOP2B expression was unaffected.
results.evaluation: The genetic screen is well-designed using haploid cells to facilitate identification of recessive mutations (C52). The resistance phenotype is confirmed with IC50 measurements showing 9-fold increase (C53), and MDR is excluded by lack of nocodazole resistance (C54). RNA-seq analysis systematically identified TOP2A as the only gene mutated in all clones (C55), with specific mutations characterized (C56-C57) and protein expression confirmed (C58-C59). The convergence on TOP2A from independent clones strongly supports its role.

results.result: CXR clones showed 8- to 19-fold resistance to etoposide, a TOP2 poison, and point mutations in TOP2A decreased the amount of TOP2A cleavage complexes (TOP2Acc) following etoposide treatment, supporting that the mutations reduce TOP2A activity.
results.evaluation: The etoposide resistance (C60) provides functional validation that TOP2A mutations affect enzyme activity, as etoposide specifically targets TOP2. The heparin-based extraction assay (C62) directly demonstrates reduced TOP2Acc formation in mutant clones, providing mechanistic evidence. The inference that mutations reduce TOP2A activity (C61) is well-supported by these complementary approaches.

results.result: Five F14512-resistant clones carried five different TOP2A mutations, all distinct from CXR mutations, confirming TOP2A as the mediator of F14512 cytotoxicity. All F14R clones showed cross-resistance to CX-5461 (3.6- to 16.8-fold), indicating that TOP2A mutations confer resistance to both compounds despite affecting TOP2A activity differently.
results.evaluation: The independent selection for F14512 resistance yielding TOP2A mutations (C63-C64) provides strong orthogonal validation of TOP2A's role. The different mutation spectrum (C65) suggests distinct mechanisms (C66), yet cross-resistance to CX-5461 (C67-C68) demonstrates convergence on TOP2A as the critical target. This bidirectional cross-resistance strengthens the conclusion that TOP2A is the primary effector.

results.result: TOP2A mutant clones showed no significant differences in proliferation rate, survival to camptothecin or calicheamicin, DNA-PK inhibitor sensitization, or DSB repair kinetics after irradiation compared to wild-type cells. TOP1 levels were also unaffected, indicating that resistance is not due to changes in proliferation or DNA repair mechanisms.
results.evaluation: These control experiments (C69-C74) systematically exclude alternative explanations for the resistance phenotype. The normal proliferation, intact HR and NHEJ pathways, and unchanged TOP1 levels demonstrate that resistance is specifically due to TOP2A mutations rather than secondary effects. This strengthens the specificity of the TOP2A finding (C75).

results.result: All CXR clones showed cross-resistance to pyridostatin (PDS) with 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher IC50 values, and all F14R clones were also resistant to PDS. siRNA-mediated depletion of TOP2A conferred marked resistance to both CX-5461 and PDS. However, TOP2A mutant cells showed no differential response to other G4 ligands (RHPS4 and PhenDC3), indicating TOP2A is specifically involved in cytotoxicity of CX-5461 and PDS.
results.evaluation: The bidirectional cross-resistance between CXR and F14R clones to both PDS and CX-5461 (C76-C77) strongly supports a common mechanism. The siRNA validation (C78) confirms this is due to TOP2A. The lack of cross-resistance to other G4 ligands (C79) demonstrates specificity and rules out general G4-related mechanisms, supporting the conclusion (C80) that TOP2A specifically mediates CX-5461 and PDS cytotoxicity.

results.result: Short treatments with PDS or CX-5461 induce rapid γH2AX and 53BP1 foci production, which is increased by DNA-PK inhibition, indicating repair through NHEJ. In CXR cells with TOP2A mutations, γH2AX production was significantly reduced. Pre-incubation with the TOP2 catalytic inhibitor BNS-22 significantly decreased γH2AX foci, demonstrating the major role of TOP2 catalytic activity in DNA break production.
results.evaluation: The DSB marker induction (C81) is well-established. The DNA-PKi experiment (C82-C83) demonstrates NHEJ involvement and validates the assay. The reduced γH2AX in TOP2A mutant cells (C84) directly links TOP2A to DSB formation. The BNS-22 inhibitor experiment (C85-C86) provides pharmacological validation that TOP2 catalytic activity is required, complementing the genetic evidence.

results.result: In TOP2A-depleted cells, γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment and strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment. TOP2B depletion did not impact PDS-induced γH2AX but reduced CX-5461-induced γH2AX to a similar extent as TOP2A depletion. Simultaneous TOP2A and TOP2B knockdown further decreased CX-5461-induced γH2AX. These results indicate TOP2A is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands, with TOP2B variably contributing depending on ligand class.
results.evaluation: The siRNA depletion experiments (C87-C91) systematically dissect the contributions of TOP2A and TOP2B. The differential effects on PDS (TOP2A-dependent only) versus CX-5461 (both isoforms contribute) are clearly demonstrated. The additive effect of double knockdown for CX-5461 (C91) supports independent contributions. The conclusions (C92-C93) are well-supported by the data, though the mechanism of differential isoform involvement remains unclear.

results.result: Using a heparin-based extraction immunofluorescence assay, the authors showed that etoposide, CX-5461, and PDS all induced significant increases in TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals. The non-clastogenic G4 ligand 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced TOP2Acc and γH2AX induction by CX-5461 and PDS but not by etoposide, supporting that these G4 ligands mediate cytotoxicity through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
results.evaluation: The heparin extraction assay is validated with etoposide (C94) before application to G4 ligands (C95). The observation of TOP2Acc formation supports the poisoning mechanism (C96). The 360A competition experiment (C97-C101) is elegant: as a non-clastogenic G4 binder, 360A should compete for G4 binding but not poison TOP2. The selective inhibition of G4 ligand effects but not etoposide effects strongly supports G4-dependent TOP2 poisoning.

results.result: Using 3D-SIM super-resolution microscopy, CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced significant increases in colocalization between BG4-detected G4 structures and TOP2Acc. This increase was not observed in etoposide-treated cells, supporting that TOP2-dependent DSBs induced by CX-5461 and PDS are associated with G4 structures in cells.
results.evaluation: The 3D-SIM colocalization approach (C102-C103) provides direct spatial evidence linking TOP2Acc to G4 structures. The specificity is demonstrated by lack of increased colocalization with etoposide (C104), which induces TOP2Acc but not in a G4-dependent manner. The speculation about etoposide increasing G4 through supercoiling (C105) is reasonable but not critical to the main conclusion (C106), which is well-supported by the colocalization data.

results.result: PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases, and EdU staining confirmed DNA damage induction by PDS and CX-5461 occurs outside of S phase. Comparison of γH2AX foci in EdU-negative versus total cells indicated that DNA replication-independent processes are very efficient for DSB production by PDS.
results.evaluation: The cell cycle analysis (C107) and EdU incorporation studies (C109) clearly demonstrate that G4 ligand-induced damage is not restricted to S phase. The quantitative comparison in EdU-negative cells (C110) provides evidence for replication-independent mechanisms. The inference (C108) is well-supported, distinguishing these G4 ligands from replication-dependent DNA damaging agents.

results.result: DSB production by PDS was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II transcription by DRB, without impeding G4 accumulation. DRB also reduced CX-5461-induced DSBs, though to a lesser extent. Pre-treatment with the RNA-Pol I inhibitor BMH21 significantly reduced CX-5461-induced γH2AX, and concomitant inhibition of both RNA-Pol I and II strongly reduced DSB production by CX-5461. These data support a key role of transcription in DSB production following G4 stabilization.
results.evaluation: The DRB experiments (C111, C113) demonstrate transcription-dependence, with the control showing G4 still form (C112), ruling out that DRB simply prevents G4 formation. The BMH21 experiments (C114-C115) reveal CX-5461's dual dependence on both RNA-Pol I and II, consistent with its known RNA-Pol I inhibitory activity. The conclusion (C116) is well-supported, though the precise mechanism linking transcription to TOP2-mediated breaks requires further investigation.

results.result: CX-5461 and PDS provoke rapid R-loop accumulation, which has been associated with transcription-dependent DSBs. Expression of RNaseH1, which resolves R-loops, caused a significant decrease in DNA damage signals induced by both G4 ligands, indicating that R-loop production contributes to DNA break formation following G4 stabilization and that transcription elongation plays a key role.
results.evaluation: The R-loop involvement is supported by prior literature (C117-C118) and directly tested with RNaseH1 overexpression (C119). The significant reduction in DNA damage upon R-loop resolution (C120) demonstrates R-loop contribution to the mechanism. The conclusion (C121) integrating transcription elongation is well-supported, though R-loops may be one of multiple mechanisms linking transcription to DSBs.

results.result: shRNA-mediated depletion of TOP1 caused a significant increase in DNA damage induced by CX-5461 and PDS, which was dependent on TOP2 activity and transcription. TOP1 depletion increased cytotoxicity of both ligands, which was reverted by transcription inhibition. These results support that a key factor in TOP2-mediated DNA damage by clastogenic G4 ligands is the accumulation of transcription-provoked topological stresses that are countered by TOP1.
results.evaluation: The TOP1 knockdown experiments (C122) reveal an unexpected protective role for TOP1. The dependence on TOP2 (C123-C124) and transcription (C126) is well-demonstrated. The cell cycle independence (C125) rules out replication-related effects. The cytotoxicity experiments with transcription inhibitor rescue (C127-C128) provide functional validation. The conclusion (C129) integrates these findings into a coherent model of transcription-induced topological stress.

results.result: TOP1 knockdown provoked a significant increase in BG4 signal with no cumulative effect of PDS and TOP1 depletion, indicating that transcription-dependent negative supercoiling from TOP1 depletion has a major impact on G4 formation. Kinetic studies showed TOP1 depletion significantly accelerates PDS-induced DNA damage signal formation, indicating TOP1 depletion facilitates DSB production by G4 ligands.
results.evaluation: The increased BG4 signal upon TOP1 depletion (C130) with lack of additivity with PDS (C131) suggests TOP1 depletion and PDS work through the same pathway of G4 stabilization. The inference about topological stress (C132) is mechanistically sound. The kinetic acceleration (C133-C134) provides temporal evidence that TOP1 loss facilitates the damage pathway, supporting the protective role of TOP1.

results.result: TOP1 activity is enhanced by BRD4-dependent phosphorylation of RNA-Pol II CTD, and BRD4 associates with PTEF to promote transcription elongation. BRD4 depletion provokes R-loop accumulation and transcription-dependent DNA damage. Inhibition of BRD4 by JQ1 provoked a significant increase in PDS-induced DNA breaks, indicating that inhibition of transcription elongation facilitates DSB formation upon G4 ligand treatment. These results suggest TOP1 antagonizes G4 ligand action through a transcription-dependent mechanism related to RNA polymerase stalling.
results.evaluation: The BRD4 background (C135-C137) establishes the connection between transcription elongation and topological stress. The JQ1 experiment (C138) demonstrates that impairing elongation increases G4 ligand-induced damage, supporting the model. The inference (C139) is well-supported. The conclusion (C140) integrates TOP1 and transcription elongation into a coherent mechanism, though the precise molecular details remain to be elucidated.

results.result: The genetic approach using chemical mutagenesis in haploid cells successfully identified TOP2A mutations despite TOP2A being essential. The nine point mutations are broadly distributed across TOP2A domains, indicating resistance can be obtained through different protein modifications not strictly dependent on catalytic function. Four mutations overlap with those conferring Vosaroxin resistance in yeast, supporting that some mutations alter TOP2A activity.
results.evaluation: The methodological discussion (C141-C142) appropriately highlights the strength of the haploid genetic approach. The observation about mutation distribution (C143-C144) is important for understanding TOP2A function. The comparison to Vosaroxin resistance mutations (C145-C147) provides external validation and mechanistic insight, though the exact functional consequences of each mutation remain to be determined.

results.result: A major finding is the differential contribution of TOP2 isoforms to cytotoxicity induced by PDS and CX-5461. While prior work showed TOP2A's role in CX-5461-induced DSBs, the impact on PDS-induced DSBs was unclear. This study shows TOP2A single-point mutations confer resistance to both ligands, confirmed through RNA silencing in HAP1 and HeLa cells.
results.evaluation: The discussion appropriately positions the findings (C148) relative to prior work (C149-C150). The demonstration that TOP2A mutations and depletion confer resistance to both ligands (C151-C152) is a clear advance, particularly for PDS where the TOP2A role was previously unclear. This represents a significant contribution to understanding G4 ligand mechanisms.

results.result: The main role of TOP2A in producing transcription-associated DNA breaks is initially surprising since TOP2B is considered the principal TOP2 for resolving transcription-associated topological stress, while TOP2A is believed to mainly resolve replication and segregation constraints. However, some studies implicate TOP2A in transcription, its activity is required for maximal transcription-dependent breaks by etoposide, genome-wide analysis shows TOP2A enrichment on highly transcribed loci, and elevated transcription promotes G4 formation favored by negative superhelicity from RNA-Pol progression.
results.evaluation: The discussion appropriately addresses the apparent paradox (C153-C154) and reconciles it with existing literature (C155-C158). The integration of prior findings about TOP2A in transcription, its enrichment at transcribed loci, and the connection to transcription-induced supercoiling and G4 formation provides a coherent framework for understanding the results.

results.result: DRB treatment completely abrogates PDS-induced DSB formation and significantly reduces CX-5461-induced DNA breaks. DNA breaks induced by CX-5461 are strongly reduced when both RNA-Pol I and II are inhibited, indicating important contribution of rDNA transcription. This is consistent with prior findings that active rDNA transcription enhances CX-5461 sensitivity and DNA damage.
results.evaluation: The transcription inhibitor experiments (C159-C161) clearly demonstrate transcription-dependence with differential contributions of RNA-Pol I and II for the two ligands. The inference about rDNA contribution (C162) is well-supported by the combined inhibitor data. The consistency with prior work (C163) strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: Topological stresses induced by transcription are mainly resolved by TOP1. This study shows TOP1 plays a major role in countering DNA break formation by CX-5461 and PDS, consistent with findings that TOP1 depletion in yeast drives genomic instability at highly transcribed G4-forming sequences. The study also demonstrates that impairing RNA-Pol II progression by inhibiting BRD4 increases PDS-induced DSBs.
results.evaluation: The TOP1 findings (C164-C165) are well-supported by the experimental data. The consistency with yeast studies (C166) provides evolutionary conservation. The BRD4 inhibition result (C167) further supports the model linking transcription elongation, topological stress, and G4-mediated damage. Together, these establish TOP1 as a key protective factor.

results.result: Inhibition of BRD4 and TOP1 activities and reduction of RNA-Pol elongation promote R-loops, which are associated with transcription-dependent DNA breaks. Expression of RNaseH1 provokes significant decrease in G4 ligand-induced DSBs. G4-forming sequences are highly correlated with R-loop-forming regions, suggesting some DSBs induced by G4 ligands are associated with R-loop formation, consistent with recent reports.
results.evaluation: The integration of R-loop biology (C168-C169) with the experimental RNaseH1 data (C170) is well-supported. The correlation between G4 and R-loop regions (C171) provides a mechanistic link. The inference (C172) is reasonable given the data, and consistency with recent literature (C173) strengthens the conclusion. However, R-loops may be one of multiple contributing mechanisms.

results.result: G4 ligands affect cell growth through multiple mechanisms. While their differential impact on targets is probably related to chemical structure affecting activity/localization (e.g., RHPS4's mitochondrial translocation due to positive charge), this study indicates CX-5461 and PDS cytotoxicity mainly relies on TOP2-dependent DNA break formation, arguing for structural determinants that block TOP2 during its active cycle. Competition experiments with 360A showed G4 stabilization alone is insufficient to provoke TOP2-dependent breaks.
results.evaluation: The discussion appropriately contextualizes G4 ligand diversity (C174-C176). The conclusion about CX-5461 and PDS mechanism (C177) is well-supported by the study data and recent literature. The inference about structural determinants (C178) is reasonable. The 360A competition experiment (C179) provides critical evidence that G4 binding alone is insufficient, supporting the concept of structure-driven TOP2 poisoning.

results.result: CX-5461 is a quarfloxin derivative, originally from the fluoroquinolone family showing dual TOP2 inhibitor and G4-binding activities. Although global TOP2 poisoning activity of quarfloxin derivatives is attenuated by increased G4 selectivity, the authors assume in their model that CX-5461's TOP2 poisoning activity is restricted to G4-forming regions.
results.evaluation: The chemical background (C180-C182) is well-established. However, the assumption that TOP2 poisoning is restricted to G4 regions (C183) is speculative and not directly tested. While consistent with the data, alternative explanations (e.g., preferential but not exclusive G4 region activity) are not ruled out. Direct genome-wide mapping of TOP2Acc would be needed to confirm this assumption.

results.result: Inhibition of DNA-PKcs dramatically increases DNA break signals in PDS and CX-5461-treated cells, demonstrating that an important number of G4 ligand-induced breaks are repaired through NHEJ. This suggests most breaks are efficiently repaired by NHEJ, while some TOP2-dependent breaks refractory to repair probably cause toxicity.
results.evaluation: The DNA-PKi experiment (C184) clearly demonstrates NHEJ involvement in repairing G4 ligand-induced breaks (C185). The inference about efficient NHEJ repair (C186) is reasonable. However, the speculation about repair-refractory breaks causing toxicity (C187) is not directly tested and represents a hypothesis for future investigation.

results.result: Based on the study results and recent reports, the authors propose a model in which CX-5461 and PDS act as 'G4-dependent TOP2 poisons.' In this model, interaction with DNA is facilitated by transcription-provoked topological stress, and G4 stabilization in transcriptionally active loci provokes sustained RNA-Pol arrest, mobilizing topoisomerases that may be poisoned near G4. The model unifies topoisomerase poisoning and G4-binding properties in the concept of DNA structure-driven topoisomerase poisoning at G-rich transcribed sequences.
results.evaluation: The proposed model (C188-C191) effectively integrates the major findings: TOP2A dependence, transcription requirement, TOP1 protective role, G4 association, and R-loop involvement. The model is well-supported by the experimental data, though some mechanistic details remain to be elucidated. The concept of 'structure-driven TOP2 poisoning' represents a significant conceptual advance in understanding G4 ligand mechanisms.
